Can you explain more about which system and which FRU device you are supporting with this and how this would be used?

It looks like the mechanism is explained fairly well but i am not understanding why someone would not just use a regular i2c eeprom to create their inventory.

Sorry for late reply, and thank you for your response.

This is intended for systems where FRU information is provided via NFC tags
rather than a traditional I2C EEPROM interface. For example, in Anacapa server
platform deployments, NFC tags are attached to FRU to allow identification 
(such as slot location) without requiring direct electrical connectivity.

In this case, the NFC tag stores binary data encoded in IPMI FRU format
inside an NDEF MIME record. BMC enables NFC driver (nxp-nci) and
uses neard to retrieve the tag records over D-Bus. This parser then decodes
the FRU payload and exposes it via xyz.openbmc_project.NfcFruDevice.

Regarding the question about using a regular I2C EEPROM:
In this design, the FRU data is intentionally encoded in the NFC tag
(as an NDEF MIME record) and retrieved via the NFC interface,
rather than being stored on a physical EEPROM.

This is used for identification purposes (e.g. slot location),
where the NFC tag is attached to the FRU and serves as the source of inventory data.

So this is not intended to replace the existing fru-device (I2C EEPROM) flow,
but to support systems where FRU information is provisioned via NFC by design.

I will add more commit message to explain it.
Thanks for explaining further, together with the other discussion thread, it starts to make sense to me how this could be used 👍

I'm a little confused about this service and its intent.  Especially because we're adding a new service, there should be some documentation (could be in your commit message if you wanted) about what this is doing.

Right off the bat, I'm not really understanding why we're adding a service to parse dbus records, and expose different dbus records.  This sounds like something that should be just done in the primary service, exposing the decoded data.

Please also link what service is hosting the nfc tag objects on dbus in this case, and overall architecture of how this is supposed to work.

Sorry for late reply, and thank you for the feedback.

This service is intended for systems where FRU information is provided via NFC tags rather than the traditional I2C EEPROM interface.

The flow is:

NFC Tag (IPMI FRU payload in NDEF MIME record)
↓
neard (exports NFC tag records on D-Bus)
↓
nfc-fru-parser (parses NDEF payload and exposes FRU inventory data on D-Bus)

The NFC tag stores binary data encoded in IPMI FRU format within an NDEF MIME record. The BMC uses NFC driver (nxp-nci) together with neard to access the tag contents. neard exposes the NDEF records on D-Bus, and this service parses the FRU payload and publishes the decoded inventory information through xyz.openbmc_project.NfcFruDevice.

This is not intended to replace existing fru-device service. It supports platforms where FRU information is intentionally provisioned via NFC tags and retrieved through the NFC stack.

The reason this is implemented as a separate service is that neard only provides generic NFC/NDEF functionality and exposes raw NDEF records on D-Bus. It has no knowledge of IPMI FRU semantics or OpenBMC inventory models. This service is responsible for interpreting a specific NDEF MIME payload format and translating it into OpenBMC inventory objects.

One example is Anacapa platform, where NFC tags are attached to FRUs and used for identification purposes (such as slot location) without requiring direct electrical connectivity.

I agree that the current commit description does not provide enough architectural context. I will add more commit message to explain it.

> The reason this is implemented as a separate service is that neard only provides

Why is this a problem?  Go add support for what you need to that service and get the maintainers to review it?

> It has no knowledge of IPMI FRU semantics or OpenBMC inventory models.

What does OpenBMC inventory have to do with this?  EM will continue hosting the inventory, all neard needs to do is publish SOME reasonable interface that EM can consume the properties of.



I will say, this hardware architecture is really odd.  IF we're going to go create our own service, lets create our own service.  No need to try to play nice with neard.  Has there been any discussion with the neard maintainers about this structured data you've put in the nfc tags?  I'd almost prefer we maintain a fork of neard, or just have a service that goes direct kernel->dbus than try to go reinvent a middleware service, but that's a discussion for after we've had some discussion there.

Just so I understand, what part of the "hardware architecture is really odd"?

I don't know that we can change much of this at this point, but the rack has NFC chips that identify rack position.  The server reads the NFC to figure out where it is in the rack.

There were two proposals for the data in the NFC: a raw string like "P12", or IPMI formatted data.  We went with IPMI data because that seemed more likely to be generally applicable, it would reuse a bunch of fru-device support (hopefully), and we'd get error detection over a raw string.

I highly suspect neard would not be interested in IPMI parsing of the NFC data, so we have to either go directly to the NFC kernel APIs or put that parsing middleware somewhere.

Loading an IPMI fru into some random field of a non IPMI protocol is really what keyed as different to me.  That's not to say we shouldn't try to support it, but I have yet to see PCIe slots identified by NFC, certainly also not with IPMI frus loaded on a field there.

FWIW, the raw "P12" string option would've meant we wouldn't have needed any implementation here, we could just have EM directly probe on Neard, but oh well, if that decision is made, we can figure that out.
Overall would like some understanding (in the commit message) of what this is doing.
I will add more commit message to explain it.

This looks like it's pulling from bluez?

No, this is not related to BlueZ.

These constants correspond to D-Bus interfaces defined by neard,
which is the NFC manager in the Linux NFC stack. For example,
"org.neard.Record" is the interface used by neard to expose
NDEF records over D-Bus.

This code simply consumes those interfaces to retrieve NFC tag
records, rather than defining a new protocol or reusing anything
from BlueZ.
Done

I'm struggling quite a bit understanding why we're trying to decode an Mime payload as an IPMI fru.  They're different formats and specifications.  If this is some off-spec usage of that, at least a rudimentary description of that needs to go in your commit message.

MIME record here is only the NDEF carrier type used by the NFC stack.
The payload inside that MIME record is vendor-defined and, in this case,
 contains binary data encoded in IPMI FRU format.

So this code is not treating MIME itself as an IPMI FRU format.
Rather, it is decoding the payload of a MIME-type NDEF record, 
where the payload content is intentionally provisioned as IPMI FRU binary data.

I agree this was not explained clearly enough in the commit message,
and I will update it to describe that layering and the intended use case.
Done

I am wondering if it makes sense to create a whole new service, executable and process here.

From what i read so far we are creating a single match from `main()` function, and not much else happens unless that match triggers.

If we just integrated the whole thing into an existing binary, there could be savings in overall compressed rofs size.

IMO conceptually it would fit into the FruDevice binary. Then we could just select which one to run based on a commandline argument.

Now if we should make it a separate process, that's another question, i do not think so. But others may have a different opinion.

The main reason I separated it was to keep the functionality isolated from FruDevice and make the code easier to maintain. However, I understand the concern about adding another service and configuration option for a lightweight feature. I can look into implementing it within FruDevice if that better aligns with the project's direction.
Thanks.
